capabilities: Extract blocks of lines that start with a configurable pattern from text files outside the vault
Write extracted blocks into Markdown files at a user-defined folder path such as EPIC.ITEM.TEST
Insert blocks at numbered positions within destination files
Configure start pattern, file extensions, root folder and working folder
Switch between Version 1 and Version 2 scanners via a startup dialog
extras: Setup requires manually downloading and placing platform-specific executables in the config directory and marking them executable; the disclosure notes the plugin scans files outside the vault. Version 1 setup is documented separately in 'README V1.md'.
intentEvidence: Version 2 represents an evolution with several key improvements.
motivation: The author built Version 2 because Version 1 dropped extracted comments into the vault without a folder structure and WASM parsing was computationally expensive due to character encoding differences.
problem: Comments embedded in source code stay locked in the codebase; Obsidian has no built-in way to pull them into structured vault documentation.

relations.evidence: The previous plugin Source Scanner Version 1 extracted marked comment blocks and placed them in the vault

requires.name: Rust executables (get-comments-linux/macos/.exe) downloaded from GitHub and placed in the plugin config dir

summary: Code documentation extractor that scans text files for marked comment blocks and writes them into Markdown notes in a user-defined folder hierarchy.
